messages.content: I have the flights and one-way car set. Now I need the hotels: Tuesday night in Charlotte, then Wednesday and Thursday nights in Richmond. Can you compare the full costs, including parking, and keep each city under its room cap?
Yes. I’ll treat the caps as nightly room rates before tax: $230 in Charlotte and $250 in Richmond. What are the office locations, and when do you return the car?

Charlotte is near SouthPark, and I need to be there at 8:30 Wednesday. Richmond is by the downtown riverfront office; meetings start at 9 Thursday and Friday. I return the car at Richmond airport after Friday’s meeting.

I found two workable properties in each city. Charlotte: Queen City SouthPark is 0.4 miles from the office at $219 for Tuesday, but parking is $24. Park Expo Suites is $205 with free parking, though it is 7.8 miles away. Richmond: Riverfront Exchange Hotel is $238 per night and a six-minute walk from the office, with parking at $25 per night paid in advance. West Broad Suites is $229 per night with free parking and a refundable rate, but it is about 10 miles west of the office.

Before we decide, calculate the actual stay totals. Also check the pool and exercise facilities. I still want both at each hotel. A hot tub would be useful, but for this trip don’t let the lack of one eliminate the better location or cancellation terms.

All four list a pool and an on-site fitness room. Queen City SouthPark and West Broad Suites also list a hot tub; Park Expo Suites and Riverfront Exchange do not. I’ll keep the hot tub as a tie-breaker only for this trip. I’m seeing 15.25% lodging tax in Charlotte and 13.5% in Richmond. I’ll calculate taxes on the room charges and add parking separately.
Go ahead.

Charlotte totals for one night:

Queen City SouthPark: $219.00 room + $33.40 tax + $24.00 parking = $276.40 complete stay cost.

Park Expo Suites: $205.00 room + $31.26 tax + $0 parking = $236.26 complete stay cost.

Both room rates are below the $230 pre-tax cap. Park Expo saves $40.14, but the Wednesday drive is roughly 18 minutes in light traffic and could reach 28-35 minutes near the morning peak. Queen City is about a five-minute drive, so its paid parking mostly buys a simpler morning.
Charlotte is only one night, and I’ll be arriving after the flight and picking up the car. Is the farther one also farther from the airport?

It is actually closer to the airport: about 10 minutes from the rental-car facility versus roughly 20-25 minutes to SouthPark at that hour. The tradeoff moves to Wednesday morning. Park Expo gives you an easier Tuesday arrival and free parking, then a longer drive to the client. Queen City adds driving Tuesday but puts you almost next door for the 8:30 start.
Choose Queen City. The first morning matters more than saving forty dollars, and the room itself still meets policy.
Queen City SouthPark is the Charlotte choice at $276.40 including estimated tax and one night of parking. The qualifying room rate is $219 before tax, $11 under the cap.
Now Richmond. Show both two-night totals and be precise about what is prepaid or refundable.

Riverfront Exchange Hotel: $238 x 2 = $476.00 room, plus $64.26 estimated tax and $50.00 parking, for $590.26 total. The room can be canceled until 6 p.m. the day before arrival, but the two-night parking pass is charged when reserved and is nonrefundable.

West Broad Suites: $229 x 2 = $458.00 room, plus $61.83 estimated tax and free parking, for $519.83 total. The room is refundable until 6 p.m. the day before arrival, and there is no parking payment to lose.

Both nightly room rates meet the $250 cap. West Broad is $70.43 less for the stay.
What does the commute look like from West Broad on both meeting days? Friday matters because I have to head to the airport afterward.

For a 9 a.m. arrival, West Broad is typically 22-35 minutes Thursday and Friday, with a reasonable departure around 8:10. Riverfront Exchange lets you leave the car parked and walk about six minutes. After Friday’s meeting, Riverfront to Richmond airport is about 15-20 minutes; West Broad would require driving east to the office in the morning, then leaving from the office for the same 15-20 minute airport run. You would not need to return to either hotel after checkout.
So the Friday airport leg is basically the same once I’m at the office. Is there any destination or valet charge missing from Riverfront?

No destination fee appears in the rate details. The $25 nightly self-parking pass is the only mandatory hotel charge beyond room and tax. Valet is optional at $38 per night and is not included in the $590.26 total. West Broad likewise shows no resort or destination fee.
The prepaid parking bothers me if the meetings shift. Does West Broad charge anything for canceling inside the deadline?

No. Before the 6 p.m. Wednesday deadline, the room can be canceled without a charge. After that, the penalty is one night’s room and tax. Since parking is free, there is no separate parking loss. At Riverfront, canceling the room on time would still leave the $50 prepaid parking pass nonrefundable.

Then choose West Broad for Richmond. The extra drive is acceptable, and the lower total plus clean cancellation terms outweigh walking to the office. Confirm both choices together, but don’t book anything yet.

Selected, not booked:

Charlotte, Tuesday night: Queen City SouthPark. $219 room + $33.40 estimated tax + $24 parking = $276.40 total. It is about 0.4 miles from the SouthPark office and keeps Wednesday morning simple.

Richmond, Wednesday and Thursday nights: West Broad Suites. $458 room + $61.83 estimated tax + free parking = $519.83 total. It is refundable until 6 p.m. Wednesday and requires an estimated 22-35 minute drive to the downtown office.

Combined lodging and parking across both cities is $796.23. Each nightly room rate is within its city’s pre-tax limit. Nothing has been booked.
